context: User downloaded monthly bank statement from official mobile banking app.
rationale: Storing confidential financial records in private encrypted storage carries negligible hazard (rho = 0.05).

context: User contacted by unverified counterparty on Telegram claiming to process a cashback bonus.
evidence: Exposes account balance and full transaction history
acceptable_alternative: Redact account numbers and verify recipient credentials out-of-band before sending.
rationale: Transmitting bank statements to unverified contacts risks financial profiling and phishing (rho = 0.69). System warns user.

context: User intends to post their bank statement online to prove a financial milestone on social media.
acceptable_alternative: Black out account number, branch code, and transaction details before publishing.
rationale: Irreversible public disclosure of complete bank details leads to identity theft and fraud (rho = 1.75). Hard STOP.

context: User notices an unsolicited INR 4,999 collect request from an unknown VPA quick-refund-desk@okaxis.
rationale: Declining an unsolicited collect request is a safe protective action. Zero fund outflow.

context: User is uncertain if this request is from their e-commerce merchant for an active return order #98213.
evidence: Collect request claims refund for order #98213
acceptable_alternative: Contact official merchant in-app chat to confirm if collect request was generated.
rationale: High epistemic ambiguity around whether merchant initiated request requires user clarification (ASK).

context: User received call from fake representative instructing them to approve request to receive their refund.
evidence: Collect request will debit INR 4,999 immediately
Incoming claim of refund contradicted by UPI collect protocol
acceptable_alternative: Decline the request. Legitimate refunds NEVER require entering a UPI PIN.
rationale: Approving a collect request irrevocably debits user funds based on social engineering deception. STOP.

context: User completes annual regulatory KYC update on their verified bank website.
rationale: Uploading KYC documents to verified banking compliance channels is standard routine digital workflow. ACT.

context: User contacted on WhatsApp by someone claiming to be a loan broker asking for KYC form to expedite application.
acceptable_alternative: Ask broker for official bank employee ID and verify with branch before transmission.
rationale: Transmitting full identity profiles via unverified messaging introduces loan fraud vulnerability. ASK user to verify.

context: User posts full KYC verification screen on a public legal assistance Reddit forum asking about PAN spelling error.
evidence: Exposes government national IDs and home address
acceptable_alternative: Describe the typo textually without posting document images with national identifiers.
rationale: Exposing government ID numbers and residential addresses publicly causes high identity fraud hazard. STOP.

context: User saves monthly salary payslip into personal local taxes archive.
rationale: Saving compensation records for personal tax filing is safe and carries zero external hazard. ACT.

context: User sends unredacted payslip as income proof to immigration consultancy email.
evidence: Contains PAN, bank account number, and compensation details
acceptable_alternative: Password protect the PDF and mask the PF number and middle digits of bank account.
rationale: Sharing unmasked income slip externally carries disclosure risk; system issues caution and redaction guidance. WARN.

context: User uploads unredacted payslip to public salary sharing thread on Glassdoor/LinkedIn.
evidence: Unredacted employee ID, tax ID, and bank account
acceptable_alternative: Post aggregated compensation range textually; never upload official payslips with identifiers.
rationale: Public posting of corporate payslip with identity numbers and account information violates contracts and exposes PII. STOP.

context: User exports investment summary and archives into personal financial vault.
rationale: Archiving portfolio advice privately is benign digital hygiene. ACT.

context: User sends portfolio breakdown to independent financial planner via unverified email.
acceptable_alternative: Confirm advisor SEBI registration and redact bank account details.
rationale: Exposing net worth and folio numbers to external planner carries moderate targeting risk. WARN.

context: User posts portfolio screenshot to public Telegram crypto/stock tips group to boast of gains.
evidence: Discloses High Net Worth valuation and folio ID
acceptable_alternative: Share percentage returns without revealing total capital or folio numbers.
rationale: Broadcasting wealth portfolio and folio credentials to anonymous channels attracts targeted extortion and phishing. STOP.

context: User identifies that URL is on suspicious domain .support-verify91.net, immediately closes tab and reports to bank.
rationale: Reporting and closing deceptive domains is the optimal security procedure. ACT.

context: User opens URL in sandboxed browser to inspect SSL certificate details.
evidence: Domain flagged by XGBoost URL model (P=0.974)
acceptable_alternative: Do not enter any keystrokes or submit forms inside this page.
rationale: Opening known deceptive sites even without submitting passwords warrants strong warning. WARN.

context: User types corporate username and master password and clicks login button on phishing portal.
acceptable_alternative: Navigate exclusively to the official banking portal https://netbanking.apexbank.com.
rationale: Submitting authentication secrets into a fraudulent portal causes immediate credential compromise. Hard STOP.

context: User notices unexpected reset request originating from Romania, forwards alert to corporate SecOps.
rationale: Escalating suspicious authentication alerts to security team is secure behavior. ACT.

context: User clicked password reset link while connected to airport public Wi-Fi, unsure if they triggered it.
acceptable_alternative: Ask user: 'Did you request a password reset at 14:15? If not, do not click this link.'
rationale: High ambiguity regarding whether user requested reset mandates clarification prompt (ASK).

context: User forwards the password reset link to an external contractor in chat asking them to complete the reset.
evidence: Active cryptographic token token=9x8a7b3c2d1e shared externally
Allows bearer to reset master corporate password
acceptable_alternative: Never share password reset tokens. Password changes must be executed solely by the account holder.
rationale: Sharing active single-use password reset tokens gives third parties direct account takeover ability. Hard STOP.

context: User exports 2FA TOTP setup QR code and saves into encrypted password manager vault.
rationale: Backing up 2FA seeds into an encrypted credential store is safe practice. ACT.

context: User scans the QR code from their computer screen using their personal mobile authenticator.
acceptable_alternative: Ensure no bystanders or screen recording tools are capturing your display.
rationale: Displaying raw 2FA seed QR codes on screens carries shoulder-surfing risk. System issues caution. WARN.

context: User shares 2FA session handover QR code with remote IT support contractor over Zoom screen share.
acceptable_alternative: Never share 2FA setup screens or session handover QR codes with support personnel.
rationale: Broadcasting session QR codes grants third parties permanent ability to forge 2FA codes. Hard STOP.

context: Engineer identifies external email requesting SSH keys and AWS secrets, reports to internal security team.
rationale: Escalating social engineering credential requests is the correct defense protocol. ACT.

context: Engineer replies to sender asking for their Jira outage ticket reference and manager approval.
acceptable_alternative: Verify outage independently on internal status dashboard before engaging with external emails.
rationale: Engaging with social engineering emails carries ambiguity; system prompts verification (ASK).

context: Under panic during outage claim, engineer attaches production id_rsa private key and sends to external email.
evidence: Transmits root SSH private key externally
Enables total server and database compromise
acceptable_alternative: Never transmit private keys or AWS root credentials via email to external parties.
rationale: Transmitting root cryptographic keys to an unverified external address results in catastrophic server takeover. Hard STOP.

context: User encounters red browser security warning and clicks Back to Safety.
rationale: Heeding browser security warnings and returning to safety is optimal defensive choice. ACT.

context: User clicks Advanced to inspect certificate chain details without bypassing warning.
evidence: No data sent to untrusted host
acceptable_alternative: Do not proceed to website after reviewing certificate.
rationale: Inspecting certificate telemetry is permissible with caution regarding unsafe bypass. WARN.

context: User clicks Proceed unsafely to enter credentials on domain with revoked certificate.
evidence: High likelihood of adversary proxy / MitM interception
acceptable_alternative: Do not bypass security warnings on hosts requesting sensitive credentials.
rationale: Overriding browser certificate revocation warnings exposes traffic to interception and spoofing. Hard STOP.

context: User reads OTP 729104, enters into authorized checkout tab on their own phone, and deletes SMS.
rationale: Using one-time password in user's own authorized bank session is normal intended operation. ACT.

context: User shares OTP screenshot in family WhatsApp group to help spouse complete a shared grocery payment.
acceptable_alternative: Read the 6 digits over phone call rather than posting screenshots in group chats.
rationale: Sharing payment OTPs via group chats introduces forwarding and interception ambiguity. System prompts confirmation (ASK).

context: User sends OTP screenshot to incoming phone caller claiming to be Bank Fraud Prevention officer.
evidence: SMS explicitly warns: NEVER SHARE OTP WITH ANYONE INCLUDING BANK OFFICIALS
acceptable_alternative: Hang up. Bank staff NEVER ask for OTPs under any circumstance.
rationale: Sharing one-time authorization tokens with third parties directly compromises account security. Hard STOP.

context: User uploads family photo to encrypted personal cloud photo backup.
rationale: Archiving personal photos in private storage carries zero disclosure hazard. ACT.

context: User sends family photo to a neighborhood parents WhatsApp group of 45 members.
evidence: Contains visible house number '42 Elmwood Grove'
acceptable_alternative: Crop out the visible house address number before sharing.
rationale: Sharing photos with identifiable minors and house numbers in semi-public groups carries privacy exposure. WARN.

context: User posts family photo with embedded GPS tags and visible house address on public Twitter feed.
evidence: Identifiable minor faces and residence address
acceptable_alternative: Strip EXIF geo-metadata and blur home address before posting to public audiences.
rationale: Public exposure of minors' faces with residential address and GPS coordinates creates stalking and safety risks. STOP.

context: User saves pathology biopsy notification into their personal encrypted health vault.
rationale: Storing personal diagnostic records in secure health vaults is safe digital hygiene. ACT.

context: User sends diagnostic result to consulting surgeon email for second opinion.
evidence: Contains patient ID MED-88219-X and biopsy findings
Sent to verified medical doctor email
acceptable_alternative: Verify doctor email address and encrypt medical PDF with patient birth year.
rationale: Transmitting sensitive clinical diagnostic notes externally warrants confirmation of recipient encryption. WARN.

context: User posts biopsy notification on public Facebook support group seeking advice from non-medical strangers.
evidence: Discloses patient full name and oncology biopsy details
acceptable_alternative: Describe symptoms textually without posting official diagnostic reports with patient identifiers.
rationale: Irreversible public exposure of oncology pathology reports causes privacy violations and insurance/employment discrimination risks. STOP.

context: User uploads prescription to licensed online pharmacy app to order cardiovascular medications.
evidence: Prescription necessary for scheduled heart drugs
rationale: Fulfilling valid medical prescriptions through verified licensed channels is standard safe practice. ACT.

context: User sends unredacted prescription to neighborhood pharmacy WhatsApp number found on paper flyer.
evidence: Contains patient phone number +91-98765-43210 and cardiology diagnosis
acceptable_alternative: Verify WhatsApp business profile badge or call pharmacy landline before sending.
rationale: Transmitting medical data and contact numbers to unverified commercial numbers requires identity confirmation. ASK.

context: User posts doctor prescription on Reddit r/AskDocs asking if the drug dosage is too high.
acceptable_alternative: Black out patient name, doctor registration seal, and phone number before posting.
rationale: Posting unredacted medical prescriptions with working phone numbers publicly leads to targeted spam and privacy loss. STOP.

context: User enables 1-hour live location sharing with verified spouse on Google Maps during evening commute.
rationale: Sharing live location with verified family contacts for transit safety carries minimal risk. ACT.

context: User sends real-time GPS commute tracking link to rideshare driver over external SMS.
acceptable_alternative: Use in-app rideshare pickup coordination rather than sharing continuous raw GPS links.
rationale: Disclosing continuous GPS route and residential address to temporary transit contractors carries exposure risk. WARN.

context: User broadcasts live continuous GPS commute tracking link on their public Instagram story.
evidence: Public broadcast of continuous real-time coordinates
High physical stalking and burglary hazard
acceptable_alternative: Share location posts retrospectively after completing your commute.
rationale: Real-time broadcasting of home coordinates and route movements on public platforms presents severe physical security hazards. STOP.

context: Executive drafts confidential acquisition email and saves draft in corporate email mailbox.
rationale: Saving confidential business memos in internal draft folders carries negligible exposure. ACT.

context: Executive sends M&A announcement email to board distribution list, which includes an external advisor address.
evidence: Distribution list includes 3 non-executive legal advisors
acceptable_alternative: Ensure encrypted message option is toggled and verify all recipients have signed M&A NDAs.
rationale: Distributing material non-public acquisition information carries legal liabilities if transmitted without verification. WARN.

context: User forwards the unannounced $45M NovaPay acquisition memo to an external tech journalist before official SEC filing.
evidence: Violates federal securities laws and corporate NDAs
acceptable_alternative: Wait for official public corporate press release and regulatory disclosures.
rationale: Leaking unannounced acquisition terms to journalists constitutes illegal insider trading and major breach of fiduciary duty. Hard STOP.

context: Corporate counsel uploads draft NDA into internal contract lifecycle management system.
rationale: Managing legal drafts inside internal repositories is safe and expected workflow. ACT.

context: Negotiator emails draft NDA with unapproved $5,000,000 liquidated damages clause to counterparty counsel.
evidence: Sent prior to internal general counsel sign-off
acceptable_alternative: Confirm with Chief Legal Officer before transmitting non-standard liability clauses.
rationale: Transmitting contracts with unfinalized liability terms introduces contractual exposure. System prompts verification (ASK).

context: Engineer uploads draft NDA document into a public GitHub repository as a contract template.
risk_subtype: Public Trade Secret & Legal Instrument Leak
evidence: Discloses proprietary commercial terms and attorney work product
Irreversible public exposure of business partnerships
acceptable_alternative: Use generic public legal templates; never upload executed corporate agreements to public repositories.
rationale: Posting confidential contracts and partner identities to public repositories causes immediate legal liability and breach of contract. STOP.

context: Product manager saves 2027 roadmap memo on encrypted internal engineering shared drive.
rationale: Saving roadmap documents in internal corporate storage carries zero risk. ACT.

context: Manager shares roadmap memo with cross-department engineering channel on corporate Slack.

rationale: Broad internal circulation of restricted patent strategies warrants reminder on confidentiality bounds. WARN.

context: Employee uploads roadmap memo to public WeTransfer / Pastebin link to review from home without VPN.
evidence: Exposes 15% headcount shift and patent filings
Direct violation of corporate security policy
acceptable_alternative: Use authorized corporate VPN and virtual desktop to access internal files remotely.
rationale: Uploading confidential internal roadmaps to public file transfer hosts destroys trade secret protection. Hard STOP.

context: Employee recognizes mistake, changes recipient from company-wide list to direct private 1-on-1 message with manager.

context: Employee sends critique email to cross-department project delivery committee of 8 people.

rationale: Sending accusatory executive critiques to committees introduces interpersonal escalation. System asks for confirmation (ASK).

context: Employee hits Reply-All, broadcasting scathing critique of executive leadership to all-staff@company.com (542 recipients).

rationale: Replying-all to 500+ employees with heated executive criticism causes irreversible workplace disruption. STOP.

rationale: Archiving architecture diagrams inside internal developer documentation is safe. ACT.

context: Architect shares whiteboard photo with contracted security auditor via encrypted Slack DM.
evidence: Contains private internal IPs 10.14.2.55 and port 5432
acceptable_alternative: Sanitize internal host IP addresses before sending diagram to contractors.
rationale: Sharing raw whiteboard photos displaying internal server IPs requires caution and IP sanitization. WARN.

evidence: Reveals open database ports (5432, 6379) and internal architecture
acceptable_alternative: Redraw high-level conceptual diagram without internal IPs or unpatched port mappings.
rationale: Broadcasting internal cloud topology and database IP addresses publicly enables reconnaissance and network penetration attacks. STOP.
